raw_response:
I am old now, and I farm the way I know from many years here in Quzhou. I cannot run too much land by myself, so this year I will keep the main part in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest way to have grain and some cash. Cotton takes more watching and more hand work when picking, so I will only keep a small piece in cotton, not too much. I have 10.1 mu total, so I plan about 7.1 mu for wheat-maize and 3.0 mu for cotton. Wheat and maize on the same land is what I have done many years. If I change too much at my age, I may lose more than I gain.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like people here usually do. I use ordinary local seed I can buy nearby, not expensive fancy seed. Before sowing I will put some compound fertilizer and a bit of urea. If the wheat looks weak after winter, I will topdress once at jointing. Water costs money, but if I skip watering and the wheat gets dry, yield falls fast, so I still plan two irrigations, one after sowing or before winter depending on soil moisture, and one around jointing. For maize, after wheat harvest I must plant quickly, so I will not do heavy tillage, just simple rotary tillage or direct seeding with a hired machine if I can get one. I use hybrid maize seed because maize seed saved at home is not reliable. I will put fertilizer mostly once at planting, maybe a small extra urea topdress if rain is good and the crop color is pale. Cotton I keep on a smaller area because it needs more hand labor and I am alone. Cotton can bring cash, but if labor is short it becomes a burden. So I plant only 3 mu, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate a couple times if dry, and spray only when I really see insects. I must leave some cash in hand, so I will not push fertilizer too high on any crop.
